product: Shnuggle Toddler Bath Tub (white, light grey foam backrest)
hand_block: The only person is Grace, and only her hand and wrist are seen, exactly the hand in the hand reference images: medium-brown skin with a warm undertone, medium-length nails with a pink French tip, a glossy sky-blue silicone band ring (the birthstone ring, exactly like the ring packshot) on the ring finger and a thin gold ring with a small stone on the index finger. NO bracelets, NO watch, nothing on the wrist. The hand and wrist enter from a frame edge with the wrist touching the frame edge; the forearm stays OUTSIDE the frame (no forearm, no arm), and the hand stays small next to the tub. When the hand touches something it GRIPS it with curled fingers, never a flat palm lying on it. No face, no other people, no children, no babies.
prod_block: The tub is exactly the Shnuggle Toddler Bath in the product reference photos: one-piece glossy white plastic oval tub, a high curved back that slopes down to a low front lip, a thick rolled rim; inside the back a light-grey oval foam backrest with a tiny embossed 'shnuggle' wordmark at its top; on the outside front a grey oval pebble badge with a white lowercase 'shnuggle' logo; inside floor a smooth raised seat bump and a pattern of small thin raised circle outlines (rings, not filled dots); a small round white plug with a little pull tab set into the flat dotted floor at the FRONT (low end) of the tub, in front of the seat bump, never on top of the bump. It keeps this exact shape, size, colours and logo in every frame: no morphing, no extra text, no handles, no other parts.

scenes.R1: Setting: a bright bathroom with SAGE-GREEN glossy tiles on every wall and a corner walk-in shower with a clear glass door, chrome shower head, a light grey shower tray floor; the white tub stands out clearly against the green; soft white daylight from a window, clean neutral white balance, bright, no golden, yellow or dark tones; folded white towels, a light grey bath mat. Shot on a phone, realistic, no cinematic grading. No on-screen text.
scenes.R2: Setting: a bright bathroom with soft BLUSH-PINK tiles on every wall, a white claw-foot bathtub with chrome taps and a chrome hand shower, light grey floor tiles, a green eucalyptus plant, a light wood stool with a folded grey towel; the white tub stands out clearly against the pink; soft white daylight, clean neutral white balance, bright, no golden, yellow or dark tones. Shot on a phone, realistic, no cinematic grading. No on-screen text. SCALE: the Shnuggle is a small toddler tub, about 75 cm long; the claw-foot bathtub is a full adult bath about 170 cm long. Whenever both are seen, the Shnuggle takes up LESS THAN HALF the bath's length and clearly narrower than the bath, with lots of empty white bath around it; it never fills the bath, never touches both ends, never sticks out over the rim.

video_suffix: Fingers stay anatomically correct (five fingers). The tub never changes shape, size, colour or logo. No sound. No on-screen text.

R1.vo: One year of daily coffee could cost more than this toddler tub.

R1.video: The hand sets the coffee cup down on the ledge, lets go and leaves the frame at the bottom right; the camera slowly pushes in toward the tub.

R1.still: Medium-wide shot of the corner walk-in shower: the empty Shnuggle tub stands alone on the light grey shower tray, sage-green tiles all around.

R1.vo: But when your baby outgrows their baby tub
R1.still: Top-down on the light grey bath mat: a small plain white infant bath tub with a grey mesh newborn sling, no logo, no text, next to the Shnuggle tub, the size difference obvious.
R1.video: Slow overhead drift from the small infant tub across to the bigger Shnuggle tub; only the camera moves.

R1.vo: and the regular tub still feels too big, finding something in between is hard.
R1.still: High angle looking down into a large empty white built-in family bathtub in the same sage-green tiled bathroom, chrome tap, nothing inside it; it looks huge.
R1.video: The camera slowly cranes down and forward over the rim into the big empty bathtub; nothing moves, no people.

R1.vo: Most options I found were for babies up to around six months,

R1.video: Slow camera arc to the left around the front of the tub, the bubbles shimmer gently; only the camera moves.
